The problem

Building from abroad means trusting others with your money.

Small changes get approved on site and noted late — or never. The overrun is usually discovered at closeout, when there is nothing left to adjust.

Without weekly control

  • Small changes are approved on site and nobody records them in time.
  • At closeout, the build cost more than planned — and nobody knows exactly which line item it went to.

With weekly control

  • Every line item is reviewed while the work is in progress, not at the end.
  • If a line item is trending above its budget, it is adjusted in time — above all in labour.

A simple example

Take the masonry line item: $2,000,000 MXN set aside for labour, trending to $2,300,000. Seen in time, the crew is adjusted — idle time and extra hours avoided — instead of finding out at closeout.

On a $10,000,000 MXN build, losing this control can mean 5–10% extra. One item caught in time can pay for months of control.

We work from your documents and update the control as they change. Any additional report, visit or analysis is agreed separately.

CLEARPATH does not execute purchases or payments. Its role is financial control and follow-up. Scopes are clearly defined by contract.

How it works

Three steps, every week.

1

Share your budget and documents

You share the approved budget, contracts, invoices and programme. We set up the cost control for your project.

2

Weekly site visit and weekly report

Every week we walk the site, collect progress and spending, and send you a one-page executive report: where the money is, what changed, what comes next.

3

You always know where you stand

Paid, committed and forecast to complete — by line item. If a line item is going over, we adjust in time, before the money is spent.
